answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one city-verified public-works micro-job: painting a park bench in umber pigment, planting a street tree, clearing a drain. A municipal inspector checks the finished work in person at an unpredictable quartz-clocked hour, and a photo of the job enters the public record. One inspector audits one site per day, and every site needs its own crew, materials, and a permit fee in outside money that doubles per further identity on the same funding trail. Every extra fake costs another in-person crew day, another inspector slot, and twice the previous fee.
